content.comment_body: Has anyone worked with [product_name] PLC and Indusoft SCADA software? I am having trouble setting up the SIETH driver for communication and need help with creating addresses in the driver sheet to properly interface with the PLC. Do I have to define VM mapping in [product_name] engineering software? Any advice would be appreciated—I'm working against a tight deadline and only need feedback from a single RTD value for the SCADA software.

Basically, a [product_name] [article_no] works similarly to an S7-200. To interface, you should address DB1 and specify the address. Place your scaled sensor value in VM-memory, create a connection, and give it a try. Some software may not work with the TSAPs that [product_name] uses, so test the following: 1. Enable [product_name] Server with Operator Panel; 2. Use [product_name] Server without Operator Panel, but try various TSAPs (using more than one channel for different TSAPs). Hope this helps.

I recently completed a project using [product_name] [article_no] and Indusoft with the SIETH driver—it works well. Refer to [document]: Connecting an HMI to [product_name] ([version_no]) or check the attachment. The connection method for [article_no] and Indusoft is nearly identical to the example shown. Use the address table in this PDF when declaring tags on IWS.

Hi, via the Indusoft forum I got the following feedback: "I've used SIETH and it works fine. [product_name] version 8 has a structure similar to S7-200." The structure matches what another user mentioned earlier. Regards.

You can use MOTCP (TCP/IP); in [product_name] engineering software, you will see Modbus addresses (via tools > Select Hardware > Modbus Address Space). Don't forget to enable Modbus access in tools > Select Hardware > General and add a Modbus Server.

analysis.insight_summary: Users face difficulties integrating [product_name] PLCs with Indusoft SCADA software, particularly with configuring the SIETH driver and correct address mapping. Some users confirm communication is achievable and resembles S7-200 integration, but requires manual setup for addressing and enabling features like VM-memory, [product_name] Server, or Modbus access. Guides and documentation are useful, but users must experiment with settings due to compatibility nuances.
analysis.user_expectations: The user seeks a reliable and straightforward solution for communication between [product_name] PLC and Indusoft SCADA using the SIETH driver, along with clear step-by-step instructions for address mapping and configuration.
